drivers.name: US 10y real yield (TIPS)

observation.name: US Treasury real (TIPS) par yield 10 yr
observation.source: US Treasury daily real yield curve

drivers.mechanism: Gold pays no yield; a higher inflation-adjusted Treasury yield raises the opportunity cost of holding it. The link was strong 2008-2021 and has been looser since 2022.

evidence.note: 60-session correlation of gold returns with Δreal yield; < −0.15 counts as an active relationship.

drivers.name: US 10y nominal yield

observation.name: US Treasury par yield 10 Yr
observation.source: US Treasury daily par yield curve

drivers.mechanism: Higher nominal yields tighten financial conditions and support the dollar; the effect on metals runs mostly through real yields, so read alongside breakevens.

drivers.name: 10y breakeven inflation
drivers.mechanism: Rising inflation expectations lower real yields for a given nominal yield and raise demand for inflation hedges. Breakevens also carry liquidity and risk premia, so small moves are noise.

drivers.name: US dollar (ICE DXY)
drivers.mechanism: Metals are priced in dollars; a weaker dollar makes them cheaper for non-dollar buyers. DXY is euro-heavy — the Fed's broad trade-weighted index (FRED DTWEXBGS) is the wider measure.

drivers.name: Fed funds effective rate
drivers.mechanism: The level of policy rates sets short real yields and carry; what moves metals day to day is the *expected path* (FOMC statements, speeches, data), which this dashboard tracks through the events list and official feeds rather than a market-implied path (no free reliable source).

drivers.name: WTI crude

observation.name: WTI crude futures, NYMEX front-month (Yahoo continuous)

drivers.mechanism: Oil feeds inflation expectations (supportive) but also mining costs and, when driven by geopolitics, safe-haven demand. Direction is ambiguous without the cause of the move.

drivers.name: Copper (industrial cycle proxy)
drivers.mechanism: Roughly half of silver demand is industrial; copper is the market's read on the industrial cycle and China. Gold has little direct link.

drivers.name: Equity volatility (VIX)
drivers.mechanism: A volatility spike can lift gold as a haven, but forced deleveraging sells everything liquid, gold included (March 2020). Silver trades more like a risk asset. Direction depends on whether the stress is a liquidity event.

drivers.name: Managed-money net position, COMEX gold (disaggregated, futures only)
drivers.mechanism: Speculative net length shows how crowded the trade is. Extreme longs (top ~15% of 3 years) raise liquidation risk on bad news; extreme shorts leave room for short-covering rallies. Positions are as of Tuesday and released Friday, so this is context, not a daily catalyst.

drivers.name: Managed-money net position, COMEX silver (disaggregated, futures only)
drivers.mechanism: Speculative net length shows how crowded the trade is. Extreme longs (top ~15% of 3 years) raise liquidation risk on bad news; extreme shorts leave room for short-covering rallies. Positions are as of Tuesday and released Friday, so this is context, not a daily catalyst.

observation.name: iShares Gold Trust — ounces in trust

drivers.mechanism: Creations add metal to the trust, redemptions remove it. Δounces is an implied net metal change — not investor cash flow and not AUM (which moves with price). One fund per metal here (GLD source pending), so it is a partial read.

drivers.name: COMEX gold curve (front spread, annualized)
drivers.mechanism: Contango near the funding rate is normal. A spread collapsing toward backwardation signals near-term tightness or a lease-rate spike; that is unusual for gold and worth checking against inventories and delivery notices before drawing conclusions.

drivers.name: COMEX silver curve (front spread, annualized)
drivers.mechanism: Contango near the funding rate is normal. A spread collapsing toward backwardation signals near-term tightness or a lease-rate spike; that is unusual for gold and worth checking against inventories and delivery notices before drawing conclusions.

gold.text: Gold's modest move up (+0.52% (0.4σ of the 21-day realized daily volatility)) may partly reflect US dollar (ICE DXY).

aligned.mechanism: Metals are priced in dollars; a weaker dollar makes them cheaper for non-dollar buyers. DXY is euro-heavy — the Fed's broad trade-weighted index (FRED DTWEXBGS) is the wider measure.

context.mechanism: Gold pays no yield; a higher inflation-adjusted Treasury yield raises the opportunity cost of holding it. The link was strong 2008-2021 and has been looser since 2022.
Higher nominal yields tighten financial conditions and support the dollar; the effect on metals runs mostly through real yields, so read alongside breakevens.
Rising inflation expectations lower real yields for a given nominal yield and raise demand for inflation hedges. Breakevens also carry liquidity and risk premia, so small moves are noise.

The level of policy rates sets short real yields and carry; what moves metals day to day is the *expected path* (FOMC statements, speeches, data), which this dashboard tracks through the events list and official feeds rather than a market-implied path (no free reliable source).
Oil feeds inflation expectations (supportive) but also mining costs and, when driven by geopolitics, safe-haven demand. Direction is ambiguous without the cause of the move.
Roughly half of silver demand is industrial; copper is the market's read on the industrial cycle and China. Gold has little direct link.

silver.text: Silver's notable move up (+1.97% (0.9σ of the 21-day realized daily volatility)) may partly reflect US dollar (ICE DXY), Copper (industrial cycle proxy).

h1_gold_vs_real_yield.hypothesis: Rolling 60-session correlation of gold returns with Δ10y real yield was reliably negative 2008-2021 and has weakened toward zero since 2022.
h1_gold_vs_real_yield.source: Entrap-Io/Gold-Regime-Shift (in-sample OLS, regime split at 2022-01 chosen a priori)

h2_gold_vs_dxy.hypothesis: Rolling 60-session beta of gold returns to DXY returns; historically negative, magnitude varies by regime.

in_sample.reference: csatzky: β≈+0.2 / −0.1, adj R²≈0.10 (levels of XAG spot; ours uses futures)

out_of_sample.read: A hit rate near 50% means the in-sample fit carried no out-of-sample signal.

caveats: Correlations and betas are descriptive; both legs often react to the same news.
All conclusions are hypotheses to re-test, not rules.

sentences: Gold is slightly up today at $4,320.50 (+0.5%), -2.4% on the week and -0.5% this year.
Silver is up today at $64.71 (+2.0%), -2.8% on the week and -7.7% this year.
One ounce of gold buys 66.8 ounces of silver, so silver is expensive relative to gold by five-year standards.
The dollar is flat (-0.25%), so it is not the story today.
The futures market is closed right now, and the prices here are delayed Yahoo quotes, not official settlements.
This is the briefing for 2026-09-25, built from the data and headlines collected up to 2026-09-25 20:54 MST.
Gold's modest move up (+0.52% (0.4σ of the 21-day realized daily volatility)) may partly reflect US dollar (ICE DXY).
Silver's notable move up (+1.97% (0.9σ of the 21-day realized daily volatility)) may partly reflect US dollar (ICE DXY), Copper (industrial cycle proxy).
Next big scheduled item: Employment Situation (September 2026) on 2026-10-02 05:30 MST.
5 of today's developments were not in the previous briefing.
Nothing on the board moved enough today to count as a catalyst; the picture is set by slow-moving conditions.
For gold the fresh evidence is balanced: 1 supportive, 1 negative, 8 mixed or unstable.
For silver the fresh evidence leans supportive: 3 supportive, 0 negative, 7 mixed or unstable.
Stances are rules applied to the latest numbers, not predictions; 'mixed' usually means the historical relationship is not holding right now.
Speculators (managed money) in gold are net long 127,389 contracts as of 2026-09-22, in a normal range versus the last three years; they cut 5,727 on the week.
Speculators (managed money) in silver are net long 13,309 contracts as of 2026-09-22, in a normal range versus the last three years; they added 185 on the week.
Metal held by ETFs: the IAU gold trust has 5 readings so far (too few to call a trend); the SLV silver trust has 5 readings so far (too few to call a trend).
The futures curve: gold is in contango at about 5.3% a year and silver is in contango at about 5.3% a year. Contango near the interest rate is normal; backwardation would signal near-term tightness.
Positioning is weekly and lagged, so it explains the backdrop, not today's move.
No COMEX gold warehouse report has been dropped in yet, so there is no inventory read for gold.
No COMEX silver warehouse report has been dropped in yet, so there is no inventory read for silver.

Dealer premiums: a 1 oz Gold Eagle costs about 3.5% over spot and a Silver Eagle about 10.6% over spot. High or rising premiums mean retail demand is outrunning dealer stock; they do not move the futures price.
Inventory moves alone do not prove a shortage; read them with delivery activity and the curve.
162 items came in over the last 24 hours, boiling down to 158 distinct stories; 2 were official releases (Fed, CFTC, BEA, central banks).
41 items mention gold and 23 mention silver.
Highest-ranked right now: "IAU vs. AAAU: Which Physical Gold ETF Is the Better Buy for Investors?" (The Motley Fool) / "AI boom fails to lift gold demand, WGC says" (Mining.com).
Items marked 'headline only' were ranked from the headline alone; opinion and forecast pieces are labelled and ranked lower.
Big scheduled items in the next two weeks: Employment Situation (September 2026) on 2026-10-02 05:30 MST.
The next positioning report lands 2026-10-02 12:30 MST.
No consensus numbers are shown because there is no free licensed source; dates come from the official schedules.
Central banks bought a net 289 tonnes of gold in 2026Q2, versus 56 in 2026Q1 (published 2026-07-30).
Gold investment demand (bars, coins, ETFs) was 262 tonnes in 2026Q2.
Silver industrial use was 650 million ounces in 2026 (forecast), roughly half of all silver demand.
The silver market is projected to be in deficit by 46 million ounces for 2026 (a forecast).
These are yearly and quarterly figures from industry bodies. They describe the backdrop and never explain a single day's move.

Gold vs real yields: the relationship is moderate right now (60-day correlation -0.28). It averaged -0.26 in 2008–2021, -0.47 in 2022–23 and -0.21 since 2024, so the claim that it broke down after 2022 does not hold on this data; it weakened later, in 2024.
Gold vs the dollar: a 1% dollar rise has lately gone with a 2.4% gold move the other way, stronger than the 2008–2021 average.

The silver fair-value indicator explained only 5% of daily moves in its fitting window, but has called the direction of the next 15 sessions right 61% of the time since 2022 on 235 overlapping signals. Overlap inflates that count, so treat it as a lead worth testing, not a result.
All of this is descriptive: it measures how things have moved together, not why, and none of it forecasts.
At today's prices one troy ounce of gold is worth $4,320.50 and one troy ounce of silver $64.71 (futures, as of 2026-09-25).

Type an amount in ounces or grams to see its dollar value, or a dollar figure to see how much metal it buys. Coins and bars sell for more than this and buy back for less; the Physical tab shows today's dealer premiums.
14 of 15 collectors succeeded on their last run.
Failing: fred (RuntimeError: FRED unreachable (2 consecutive batch timeouts).
The database holds 124 series, 229,307 observations and 1,981 news items.
Known gaps: FRED is unreachable (a free API key fixes this), so yields come from the Treasury's own files; no COMEX warehouse file has been dropped in yet; GLD holdings are not collected.
